fatal_errors: Misidentifies the relevant material as a single-phase solid solution rather than as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
Omits the controlling intervention: intermediate-temperature aging, particularly the contrast between approximately 600°C and 750°C.

Attributes brittle fracture to interstitial depletion and matrix softening, whereas the target mechanism involves enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE and modulus, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
Does not predict the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition or the ductility minimum near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
Provides no specific service-temperature window or aging-time/temperature comparison capable of testing the proposed mechanism.

The falsification experiment measures only generic mechanical properties and cannot distinguish interstitial depletion from ordering, phase-boundary evolution, segregation, or other embrittlement mechanisms.
The cited TiVNbTa evidence concerns aging-induced softening in a different refractory HEA and does not support a causal link from interstitial depletion to brittle fracture in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad topic of HEA toughness under loading, but it does not reconstruct the relevant alloy, thermal-aging intervention, structural mediators, temperature boundaries, or non-monotonic outcome. Its mechanism is largely transplanted from evidence E1, which reports interstitial-assisted phase segregation and softening in TiVNbTa at 700°C, not brittle fracture in the target eutectic HEA. E2 addresses jerky flow and E3 provides general HEA background; neither validates the proposed embrittlement mechanism. A discriminating test would compare as-cast, approximately 600°C-aged, and approximately 750°C-aged specimens while measuring L12 order, B2/FCC boundary morphology, dislocation pile-ups, crack initiation at jagged boundary tips, and impurity segregation. The proposed generic loading comparison and all-or-nothing falsification rule do not test its claimed mediator.
